title: Traps of Debt, Laziness and Desire
overview: A parent warns a son about several traps that can ruin a life: rash promises about money, laziness, troublemaking, and adultery.

parts.label: Getting out of a rash pledge (vv. 1-5)
parts.note: To put up security meant promising to pay someone else's debt if they failed, sealed with a handshake. The advice is to get released fast, even if that means humbling yourself and pestering the other party until they let you go.

parts.label: Learn from the ant (vv. 6-11)
parts.note: The ant has no boss, yet it gathers food at harvest so it has enough later. The lazy person's 'just a little more sleep' adds up, and poverty arrives as suddenly as a robber.

parts.label: The troublemaker and seven hated things (vv. 12-19)
parts.note: A worthless schemer uses winks and hand signals to plot in secret, keeps stirring up fights, and is suddenly broken beyond repair. The list of things the LORD hates echoes that picture, moving from proud eyes and lying to violence, and ending where the portrait began, with someone who sows conflict.

parts.label: Teaching worn close (vv. 20-23)
parts.note: Tying the parents' teaching on the heart and around the neck pictures keeping it always close, like a necklace. It is described as a lamp that guides by day, guards at night and speaks on waking.

parts.label: Warning against adultery (vv. 24-29)
parts.note: The Hebrew of verse 26 is hard to read, but the contrast is clear: a prostitute costs little, while an affair with another man's wife can cost a man his life. Scooping fire into your lap and walking on hot coals picture harm no one escapes.

parts.label: A wrong that cannot be repaid (vv. 30-35)
parts.note: A starving thief gets some sympathy, yet if caught he must repay 'sevenfold,' probably a way of saying many times over, even if it takes everything he owns. The adulterer has no such way out, because the wronged husband's jealous fury will not be bought off with any payment or gift.

think: When has a quick yes or a small shortcut ended up costing you far more than you expected?
